newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos firmer, forwards stable, bonds bid.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos firmer, forwards stable, bonds bid.

text.p: Greek depos were trading higher as players sought funding for the upcoming auction of government securities, forex forwards were stable but for a rise in tomorrow/next, and bonds were bid in quiet trading, dealers said.
The drachma was unable to break through the 309.50 level against the ecu on the downside, trading around 309.60/65 in late dealings.
"Banks seek funding for the upcoming auction of fixed coupon bonds pulling the depo curve upward. Forex forwards are little changed but for a spike in tomnext," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The finance ministry will auction fixed coupon bonds on July 15, if it sticks to its tentative borrowing schedule released in early June.
Bonds were well bid but trading volume remained subdued, dealers said.

"We have seen very few deals but bid prices are rising," a dealer said. "It looks as if players do not want to sell bonds but prices are bid up to make a likely auction of fixed coupon bonds next week look more expensive."
The 10-year bond yield stood at 9.15 percent, the seven-year bond at 9.39 percent, the five-year bond at 9.66 percent and the three-year bond at 10.01 percent.
The mark was quoted at 157.20/30 from Monday's 157.550 fix, the dollar at 274.26/36 drachmas from 274.680 and the ecu at 309.28/38 from 309.75 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is locked in the 309.50/80 range in thin trading," said a senior forex dealer at a foreign bank. "The trend is downward but 309.50 proved again a good support level."
